name: chocolate chip cookies
instructions:
The chocolate chip cookie recipe. VARIANT A is Nicole Rucker's Classic Soft Chocolate Chip Cookies — the COLD-BUTTER, LIMITED-FRIDGE-TIME method (30-minute freeze, not an overnight rest). Future variants join as they're tested.

=== VARIANT A — NICOLE RUCKER'S CLASSIC SOFT (COLD BUTTER, LIMITED FRIDGE TIME) ===

MAKES 12 COOKIES.

INGREDIENTS:
- 2 cups (250g) unbleached all-purpose flour
- 2/3 cup packed (142g) light-brown sugar
- 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar
- 1 tsp (6g) baking soda
- 1 tsp (3g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt
- 1 tbsp (10g) cornstarch
- 4 oz (113g) COLD unsalted butter, cubed
- 1 1/3 cups (226g) bittersweet chocolate chips, + more for topping the dough balls before baking
- 1 large egg (50g)
- 1 large egg yolk (14g)
- 2 tsp (10g) vanilla extract
- 1 tbsp (12g) neutral cooking oil

PROCEDURE:
1. DRY + COLD BUTTER: in a stand mixer with the paddle, mix the flour, sugars, baking soda, salt, and cornstarch — this disperses the soda and breaks up any lumps of sugar. Add the COLD CUBED BUTTER and mix on LOW until the mixture resembles RUSTIC SAND, about 4 minutes. Add the chocolate chips; briefly mix on low to disperse.
2. WET IN SLOWLY: whisk the egg, egg yolk, vanilla, and oil together in a small bowl, and slowly add to the buttery mixture on low speed. Once all the egg is incorporated, turn the speed to medium to bring the dough together.
3. PORTION + FREEZE 30 MIN: spoon-portion the dough into TWELVE balls, press the decorative chocolate chips onto the tops, transfer to a plate or quarter sheet pan, and FREEZE, uncovered, for 30 MINUTES.
4. BAKE: while the dough chills, preheat to 375°F (190°C) and line two half sheet pans with parchment. Six balls per pan; bake both on the center racks for 10 minutes. ROTATE the pans and bake an additional 5-6 minutes, until LIGHTLY BROWNED AT THE EDGES and SET BUT DAMP-LOOKING IN THE CENTER.
5. COOL a few minutes before eating.
6. STORAGE: sealed container in the FRIDGE up to a week; for best results warm 15 seconds in the microwave. (Her note: several friends said these tasted even better after 2 days.)
notes:
=== VARIANT A SOURCE — NICOLE RUCKER ===

Her headnote: this is the soft light-brown-sugar cookie of the late 1980s — the Nestlé Toll House yellow-bag recipe or the Pepperidge Farm Soft Baked grocery-store cookie. SOFT, toothsome, and moist, but definitely not cakey. The engineering vs old-school Toll House: A BIT OF NEUTRAL OIL and A SMALL AMOUNT OF CORNSTARCH keep that soft texture — and keep it for up to a week in a sealed container.

=== THE METHOD MARKERS — COLD BUTTER, LIMITED FRIDGE TIME ===

What distinguishes variant A from standard creaming-method cookies:
- COLD CUBED BUTTER cut into the dry mix until 'rustic sand' (pie-crust logic, not creamed butter).
- LIMITED FRIDGE TIME: a 30-minute uncovered FREEZE of the portioned balls — not the overnight fridge rest most modern recipes demand.
- Egg + yolk + vanilla + oil whisked and added slowly to the sandy base.

=== DONENESS ===

Lightly browned at the edges, set but damp-looking in the center — the same pull-early discipline as [[tofu-brownie-cookies]].

=== STORAGE — RUCKER'S FRIDGE + MICROWAVE PATTERN ===

Fridge in a sealed container up to a week, 15-second microwave refresh. Third recipe in a row from her with this leftover engineering ([[pear-crumble]], [[tofu-brownie-cookies]]) — and here she claims they're even better after 2 days.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[tofu-brownie-cookies]]: the other Rucker cookie (silken tofu, double chocolate).
- [[russian-tea-cakes]]: the other cold-butter-worked-by-hand cookie.
- [[chocolate-cake]]: the chocolate-dessert neighbor.
